payload.name: Illusory Truth Effect (Fluency-Based Truth Perception)
payload.fact: Repeated or memory-retrieved statements are experienced as more fluent and familiar, leading to increased perceived truthfulness/validity compared to novel statements.
payload.boundary: Demonstrated with trivia statements, rumors, and factual statements using direct repetition and indirect polling methods; effect is logarithmic with diminishing returns for additional repetitions.

provenance.title: The Truth About the Truth: A Meta-Analytic Review of the Truth Effect
provenance.quote_or_locus: Repetition has been shown to increase subjective truth ratings of trivia statements

provenance.title: The illusory-truth effect and its absence under accuracy-focused processing are robust across contexts of low and high advertising exposure
provenance.quote_or_locus: However, when participants were instructed to adopt an accuracy focus at encoding by judging the truth of the product statements, new statements were judged to be as true as repeated statements

provenance.title: The illusory-truth effect and its absence under accuracy-focused processing are robust across contexts of low and high advertising exposure
provenance.quote_or_locus: In the test phase, repeated statements received higher truth ratings than new statements

provenance.title: Remembering makes evidence compelling: Retrieval from memory can give rise to the illusion of truth.
provenance.quote_or_locus: our experiment demonstrated that information retrieved from memory does indeed give rise to an illusion of truth

provenance.title: The effects of repetition frequency on the illusory truth effect
provenance.quote_or_locus: In both experiments, we found that perceived truthfulness increased as the number of repetitions increased. However, these truth rating increases were logarithmic in shape
